title: Ansel and the Spire
premise: Rosalind Lockridge has spent her life as a ghost—smuggling goods through the Thornfell passes for the Emberwright Guild, the last keepers of a covenant that binds the mortal realm to the dragon-fire that holds back the encroaching Hollow. When she finds tonight's date inscribed in the Vellum Codex, a century-old book of prophecies, she learns she is named as the Covenant-Bearer who must carry a dying dragon's ember across the mountains and reforge the broken pact at the Spire. Hunted by the Hollow's faceless servants, betrayed by her own guildmaster—who sold the covenant's secrets years ago to save himself—and shadowed by a prophecy-scribe's descendant who claims to know her true parentage, Rosalind must choose between erasing herself from history to survive or claiming an identity written in fire. At the Spire, she discovers the original covenant was forged by her mother, who gave her memories as payment; Rosalind reforges it by offering not her life but her name, becoming both remembered and unrecorded. The dragon-fire is renewed, the Hollow recedes, and Rosalind walks out of the Spire a stranger even to herself—free, alive, and finally choosing who she will be.
about_author: Kestrel Winterbourne is the pen name of a former mountain guide who traded trail maps for story maps after a near-fatal winter in the passes. They write fantasy about people who survive things they were never meant to survive.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. On a routine smuggling run through the Thornfells, Rosalind shelters in a ruined waystation and finds the Vellum Codex, its final page bearing tomorrow's date and her own description. The emotional beat is cold dread: the invisible life she built cracks open in a single night.

chapters.title: Emberwrights, Last of Their Name
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She returns to the guildhall to find only four Emberwrights remain, tending a guttering brazier said to hold the last dragon-fire. Guildmaster Corvane dismisses the codex as forgery, but old scribe Maren recognizes the handwriting. Beat: uneasy belonging among people clinging to a dying purpose.

chapters.title: What the Hollow Leaves
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals the covenant: dragon-fire holds back the Hollow, a hunger between realms, and the pact must be renewed at the Spire every hundred years—or never was, if the codex lies. A village at the mountain's edge is found emptied, doors open, meals half-eaten. Beat: creeping horror made intimate.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Searching guild records for the codex's origin, Rosalind finds payments in Corvane's ledger from an unknown buyer—dated the year the last renewal failed to happen. She realizes someone inside the guild wanted the covenant broken. Beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Scribe's Grandson
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Tobin Ashvale, grandson of the codex's author, arrives seeking Rosalind, carrying his grandfather's marginalia: notes on the Covenant-Bearer's identity. He believes Rosalind is more than a smuggler. Beat: reluctant alliance; being seen for the first time is terrifying.

chapters.title: Roads Only I Know
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. With Hollow servants tracking them, Rosalind leads Tobin and Maren through smuggler paths no map records. Her knowledge of hidden ways becomes their survival. Beat: competence as identity—the first time her invisibility feels like power rather than erasure.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The party reaches a shrine where dragon-fire once burned; Maren performs the old rites and the brazier ember flares, answering Rosalind's presence alone. Maren conceals what this implies about Rosalind's bloodline. Beat: wonder shadowed by a keeper's guilt over secrets kept too long.

chapters.title: The Faceless Pursuit
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Hollow agents—people whose faces are smooth as unwritten paper—ambush the party at a river ford. Maren is taken. Tobin saves the ember but freezes in combat, ashamed. Beat: fear that memory itself is what the Hollow devours first.

chapters.title: Interrogating the Past
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Grieving Maren, Rosalind presses Tobin for the marginalia's full contents and learns the Covenant-Bearer was described as 'the daughter of the forge-mother.' Her mother died when she was six; her father was never named. Beat: anger at everyone who knew and said nothing.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Flashback-chapter: twenty-five years ago, Corvane sold the covenant's rites to a Hollow intermediary to save the guild from bankruptcy, believing the prophecies were superstition. Now he sends hunters after Rosalind to bury the evidence. Beat: self-justification curdling into desperation.

chapters.title: High Pass, Thin Air
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Above the treeline, the ember dims and Rosalind must feed it something precious—a lock of hair, then a cherished memory of her mother's lullaby. The price of survival becomes literal. Beat: sacrifice as choice, grief as fuel.

chapters.title: The Paper-Faced Man
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Captured briefly by a Hollow agent, Tobin experiences the Hollow's offer: return everything you've lost, forget everything you fear. He escapes but can't stop wanting it. Beat: temptation—not evil, but relief.

chapters.title: Maren, Remembered Wrong
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They find Maren alive but hollowed—she remembers her life perfectly except anything involving Rosalind, who has been cut out of her like a bad tooth. Beat: horror that the enemy doesn't kill you; it edits you.

chapters.title: Forge-Mother
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Fragmented memories surface: Maren helped Rosalind's mother, Elira, hide the child before Elira went to the Spire to buy time for the failing covenant with her own memories and name. Rosalind learns her mother chose oblivion willingly. Beat: devastating inheritance—love measured in what was given up.

chapters.title: Corvane's Hunters
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Guild hunters corner the party in a gorge; Rosalind recognizes their leader, her oldest friend Bren, ordered to bring her back dead or discredited. She defeats him without killing him and shows him the ledger page. Beat: loyalty tested; some betrayals can be walked back.

chapters.title: The Spire Below the Ice
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. The party reaches the Spire—a tower of black glass rising through a glacier, warm to the touch. Inside, walls record every covenant-bearer's name; Elira's line ends mid-stroke, unfinished. Beat: awe and dread converging at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Hollow's Heart
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In the Spire's depths, the Hollow manifests wearing her mother's remembered face, offering Rosalind her mother's memories back if she abandons the forging. Rosalind nearly accepts. Beat: the climax of temptation—grief weaponized.

chapters.title: What Corvane Knew
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane arrives with guild remnants, intending to destroy the Spire and end the debt forever—but Bren turns on him, and the remaining Emberwrights stand with Rosalind. Corvane, confronted, breaks. Beat: the architect of ruin watching his bargain come due.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Climax. Rosalind sets the ember into the Spire's heart and offers her payment: not her life, but her name—every record, memory, and mention of 'Rosalind Lockridge' surrendered to the flame. The covenant blazes renewed; the Hollow recoils screaming into the dark. Beat: transcendence through willing loss.

chapters.title: A Stranger in Her Own Story
chapters.summary: Tobin's POV. Aftermath: the world remembers a woman left the Spire, but no one can recall her name or face—except Tobin, who wrote it down beforehand in the codex's margin, gambling on ink over memory. Beat: fragile hope; love as an act of record-keeping.

chapters.title: Names We Choose
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Recovering in the rebuilt guildhall, Rosalind reads her own name in Tobin's handwriting and must decide whether to reclaim it or take a new one. She signs the guild's new charter with a name she chooses herself. Beat: identity as authorship, not inheritance.

chapters.title: First Fire of Spring
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, mostly Rosalind's POV. The dragon-fire burns steady in every hearth the Emberwrights tend; the passes are safe again; Maren begins relearning the missing pieces, and chooses to fill them with new memories instead. Rosalind watches the sunrise over Thornfell, no longer hiding. Final beat: survival's price paid, and worth it.
